headline: Chip sell-off drags US stocks lower as volatility jumps
summary: US equities sold off broadly, led by semiconductors. Credit ETFs were comparatively resilient, but weak breadth and higher volatility left the source outlook tilted slightly towards its downside scenario.

highlights.title: Semiconductors led the decline
highlights.text: The semiconductor index fell 12.25%, while VIX rose from 16.61 to 28.18. The S&P 500 closed near its intraday low.

highlights.title: Credit held up better than equities
highlights.text: HYG slipped 0.31% and LQD rose 0.15%. Equal-weight equities fell less than the headline S&P 500; this was relative resilience, not a broad recovery.

highlights.title: Payrolls fall inside the forecast window
highlights.text: The report retained its original 18/40/42 scenario split after updating its sentiment inputs. It treats payrolls and closing moves in chips, volatility and credit as evidence to monitor.

forecast.horizon: 6–10 November US sessions · S&P 500 final close
forecast.method: Original US outlook in section 9; the source’s sentiment update did not alter its probabilities or final-close boundaries. The forecast ID is an archive locator. The issue timestamp is the verified completed Drive modification time. Subjective probabilities, not statistically calibrated.
forecast.watch_next: Watch payrolls and closing confirmation in semiconductors, volatility and credit. Mean Brier was 0.721 across 12 completed original US windows, worse than the 0.667 uniform baseline.

limitations: Curated from the source report, not independently verified. NYSE breadth was secondary, end-of-day put/call and fund flows were unavailable, and Brent settlement was media-reported. After-hours quotes were not used as forecast anchors.
